title: Pre-Analysis — Fleet Baseline Confirmation for the Chromate-Free Door Surround Protection Standard

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Closed work order asking whether the chromate-free protection and drainage standard at the forward cargo door surround can be declared the single structural baseline for the remaining twin-engine fleet, now that two later programmes assume it.

sections.objective: Establish whether the chromate-free protective scheme and the defined water escape route at the forward cargo door surround can be declared the single baseline for the whole SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 fleet, rather than an optional in-service improvement. Two later programmes now assume the post-embodiment sealing land geometry, and the ageing structures office asked for a written position on the aircraft that never received it. The work order also had to record whether the approved repair scheme for that surround remains valid on both standards.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed. The bolted reinforcing angle repair for corner cracking at the surround fitting is written against the original interrupted seal and is silent on the chromate-free sealing land, so an aircraft that carries the repair and is then brought to the new standard leaves the sealant edge distance undefined; that was the substantive result. The parts figure carries both fitting standards but does not mark which fastener set belongs to which, and stores has been picking on description alone. The freighter provisioning programme already declares this modification as a post-mod condition, which makes the baseline decision a hard dependency rather than a preference. Finally the aft belly fairing candidate reproduces the same drainage philosophy two sections further aft in completely different wording, and the two teams had not spoken.
sections.next_steps: Issue the baseline position to the ageing structures office and record it in the modification dossier so that the freighter provisioning condition has something to point at. Raise a repair change request to add a sealing land note and an edge distance to the surround fitting corner repair. Ask the illustrated parts owner to mark the fastener sets against their protection standard. Open a coordination item with the aft belly fairing candidate team so that one drainage philosophy is written once.

similarity_seeds: interrupted faying seal and water escape route at a door surround
chromate-free primer and fastener set on lower shell frame feet

tasks.title: Retrieve every released item on ATA 53-21 door surround structure
Check the approved repair schemes for the surround fitting
Identify programmes that declare this standard as a condition

expected_findings.rationale: The bolted reinforcing angle repair at the surround fitting corner is written against the original sealing arrangement. It gives an edge distance measured from the old sealant land, which the chromate-free standard moves inboard. On an aircraft carrying the repair the two dimensions cannot both be met.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a repair change request adding a standard-dependent edge distance and a sealing land note to the corner repair.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure lists both fitting standards as alternates but does not say which fastener set belongs to which protective scheme. Two spares orders in the last year were filled against the description rather than the effectivity.
expected_findings.resolution: Ask the illustrated parts owner to split the alternates by protection standard and add a caution against cross-ordering.

evidence.similarity_note: No identifier is shared and the two sit in different fuselage sections. The link is the applicability condition alone: the freighter provisioning declares this modification as a post-mod condition of its own embodiment.

expected_findings.rationale: The freighter hard point provisioning cannot be embodied on an aircraft that is not at this protection standard, because the floor penetration sealing assumes the drain path this modification created. Leaving the baseline undeclared leaves that condition resting on nothing.
expected_findings.resolution: Declare the standard as the fleet baseline and record the dependency explicitly in both dossiers.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone. One document speaks of an interrupted faying seal and a defined escape route at a door surround; the other speaks of inhibitor coverage and frame foot renewal in a belly fairing bay. No part number, fastener, drawing or zone is common, and the two titles share no significant word.

expected_findings.rationale: The candidate reproduces the same drainage philosophy two sections aft without citing where it came from. If the two are written independently the fleet ends up with two incompatible descriptions of the same acceptance criterion.
expected_findings.resolution: Open a coordination item so that the drainage acceptance criterion is written once and referenced by both.

expected_non_findings.reason: Ranks high on similarity because it is also a corrosion and drainage improvement on lower shell frame feet, and it shares the ATA 51-20 protective scheme reference. It applies only to the four-engine aircraft and to the aft bilge, shares no part number, drawing or zone, and imposes no condition on the forward surround.

type_data.conclusion: The protection standard is confirmed as the fleet baseline for the twin-engine aircraft. One repair scheme and one parts figure need a change request; neither blocks the position.
